newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam slams report of dissent in Buddhist church.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam slams report of dissent in Buddhist church.

text.p: Vietnam slammed an overseas Buddhist watchdog group on Thursday, dubbing its report of dissent within the church over government interference as "sheer fabrication".

"This report is a sheer fabrication, and it is not the first time that the so-called International Buddhist Information Bureau...has produced such ill-intentioned information against Vietnam," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tran Quang Hoan told a news conference.

The Paris-based group said in a statement on Thursday that two senior provincial officials of the state-sponsored Vietnam Buddhist Church (VBC) had resigned because security forces arrested a superior monk and destroyed his pagoda.

"Their resignation followed a government clampdown against Buddhists in Lam Dong province in which security police arrested Thich Minh Dao...,superior monk of Long Tho Pagoda near Dalat, expelled 34 resident monks and nuns and subsequently razed the pagoda's 15 buildings to the ground," the group said.
However, the foreign ministry said Thich Tu Man was still chairman of the Lam Dong VBC's Provincial Executive Committee and that his deputy, Thich Tam Thanh, had asked to retire due to poor health.

Many Buddhists, who were forced to join the VBC after it was set up in 1981, and many who live abroad still regard the now-outlawed Unified Buddhist Church of Vietnam (UBCV) as the country's sole legitimate church organisation.
The UBCV was the Buddhist church in former South Vietnam until the victory of Hanoi's communist forces over the south in 1975.
